newsitem.title: INDIA: India may offer only two more GDR issues in 1997.
newsitem.headline: India may offer only two more GDR issues in 1997.

text.p: India's state-owned monopoly firms are likely to offer only two Euroissues in the remaining months of calendar 1997 though international appetite for Indian paper is strong, merchant bankers said.
"The earliest date really is October," said one merchant banker at a London-based investment firm. "I can't see more than two issues hitting the market in 1997."
India last month said it planned to sell stakes in four firms: the Gas Authority of India Ltd (GAIL), Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd (MTNL), Indian Oil Corp (IOC) and Container Corp of India.
The privatisation drive is planned partly through an offer of global depository receipts (GDRs) to overseas investors.
Although the size of each will depend on the final pricing, the merchant banker said he expected a $700 million GDR issue by GAIL and another $800 million offering by MTNL.
"There's a substantial appetite for Indian GDRs," said Rupa Bose, strategist at Asia Equity Ltd, a fully owned subsidiary of Banque Paribas.
She said Indian GDRs listed overseas were quoted at an average premium of 15-to-20 percent over the domestic price of the underlying stock on Indian exchanges.
"Whether you get that sort of premium is a difficult call to make," she told Reuters from her office in Singapore. "The pricing depends on sentiment and demand and supply at the time of issue."
Typically, international funds allocate 15-to-20 percent of their cash to oil and gas, but there have not been Indian GDRs in these sectors, analysts said.
"There's very definite demand for oil and gas," a foreign investment banker said. "But, I don't see IOC coming through until the government resolves freer pricing policy for oil."
IOC is the sole canalising agency for the country's imports of crude oil and major petroleum products. IOC supplies nearly 55 percent of petroleum products sold in India.
But the firm is being forced to borrow heavily because the government has been unable to reimburse the firm for selling oil at subsidised rates.
Analysts said there must be a gap between the GAIL and MTNL offerings to ensure a smooth ride.
"The government must produce a sensible calendar for GDRs to make them successful," a fund manager said. "Or, both will get knocked down."

He said GDR issues in the last quarter of a calendar year would not cause problems because international funds would get fresh inflows and juggle portfolios to subscribe to what they consider attractive offerings.
The banker said a GDR issue by Container Corp was unlikely before April 1998.
So far this year, only India's overseas telecommunication monopoly, Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd, has raised $526.6 million by selling 37.8 million GDRs in March.
